answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable proof-of-personhood credential, issued only after an in-person check and renewed periodically. A reputation score is then tied to that credential, not to an account, so a newcomer cannot gain weight by spawning a plume of cheap identities or copying an established agent’s record. The anchor is the costly verification and renewal: an attacker must recruit real people and repeat the checks, paying time and money for every identity, while a whisper campaign of fake accounts still carries little influence.
